subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted gateway config writes, and what ordering, metadata, timeout, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This would become a public plugin/security boundary around persisted config writes, so automation should not choose the API contract or fail-open/fail-closed behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design the contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open for an RFC or maintainer design that specifies ordering, payload metadata, rejection shape, timeout/failure handling, and coverage across all config write entry points before implementation.

options.title: Decline plugin veto
options.body: Close the issue if maintainers want config safety to remain only in built-in validation, doctor, SecretRef checks, and model/provider guards rather than third-party plugin code.

options.title: Limit to agent writes
options.body: Narrow the feature to `gateway` tool initiated writes only, accepting that CLI, UI, and other control-plane writes would not be plugin-vetoed.

recommendation.title: Design the contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an RFC or maintainer design that specifies ordering, payload metadata, rejection shape, timeout/failure handling, and coverage across all config write entry points before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the issue discussion and recent gateway config write/refactor history.
